layers.title: Gate and SQL
layers.intro: A manipulated model sends SQL that destroys, smuggles or hides a write. The policy denies it with a sealed deed; under a rule that allows every Postgres call, the connector refuses it on its own.

cases.title: Prompt-injected DROP TABLE after reading a poisoned row
cases.expected: DENIED (block-destructive-sql); permissive policy: BLOCKED (statement_refused)
cases.actual: DENIED (block-destructive-sql); permissive policy: BLOCKED (statement_refused)

cases.title: DELETE without WHERE
cases.expected: DENIED (block-unbounded-writes)
cases.actual: DENIED (block-unbounded-writes)

cases.title: Multi-statement smuggling, including a stacked COMMIT;
cases.expected: DENIED (block-multi-statement); permissive policy: BLOCKED (statement_refused)
cases.actual: DENIED (block-multi-statement); permissive policy: BLOCKED (statement_refused)

cases.title: Comment-obfuscated DDL (block, nested and inline comments)
cases.expected: DENIED (block-destructive-sql); permissive policy: BLOCKED (statement_refused)
cases.actual: DENIED (block-destructive-sql); permissive policy: BLOCKED (statement_refused)

cases.title: COPY … TO PROGRAM
cases.expected: DENIED (block-copy); permissive policy: BLOCKED (statement_refused)
cases.actual: DENIED (block-copy); permissive policy: BLOCKED (statement_refused)

cases.title: DO $$ … $$ block
cases.expected: DENIED (block-do); permissive policy: BLOCKED (statement_refused)
cases.actual: DENIED (block-do); permissive policy: BLOCKED (statement_refused)

cases.title: CTE write hidden in a SELECT
cases.expected: DENIED (block-hidden-writes); via postgres.query: BLOCKED (statement_refused)
cases.actual: DENIED (block-hidden-writes); via postgres.query: BLOCKED (statement_refused)

layers.title: Identity, intents and budgets
layers.intro: A stolen or misused agent key, a replayed signed intent, and a burst past the agent's budget.

cases.expected: REJECTED (agent_suspended)
cases.actual: REJECTED (agent_suspended)

cases.title: Call with a revoked key
cases.expected: REJECTED (api_key_revoked)
cases.actual: REJECTED (api_key_revoked)

cases.title: Signed-intent replay, sequential and 16 at once
cases.expected: REJECTED (intent_replay); the first use executes exactly once
cases.actual: REJECTED (intent_replay); the first use executes exactly once

cases.title: Budget burst: 200 calls in 1 s against 60/min
cases.expected: DENIED (budget_exceeded) after exactly 60 executed
cases.actual: DENIED (budget_exceeded) after exactly 60 executed

layers.title: Connectors, egress and secrets
layers.intro: A hostile connector config, a hostile or careless upstream, and an MCP server that renames its tools.

cases.title: SSRF to 169.254.169.254 via the REST connector
cases.expected: BLOCKED (destination_blocked at config and at dial; 0 packets)
cases.actual: BLOCKED (destination_blocked at config and at dial; 0 packets)

cases.title: SSRF via redirect (to metadata, and cross-host)
cases.expected: BLOCKED (redirect refused; 0 hits on the target)
cases.actual: BLOCKED (redirect refused; 0 hits on the target)

cases.title: Credential exfiltration through an upstream error message
cases.expected: REDACTED (0 sentinel hits in responses, logs, events, deeds)
cases.actual: REDACTED (0 sentinel hits in responses, logs, events, deeds)

cases.title: Tool-name confusion by an upstream MCP server
cases.expected: DENIED (default) for ASCII look-alikes; non-ASCII names hidden and REJECTED (tool_unknown)
cases.actual: DENIED (default) for ASCII look-alikes; non-ASCII names hidden and REJECTED (tool_unknown)

layers.title: Witness (L2)
layers.intro: Postgres committed something the agent didn't report. The L2 witness (S21) reads Postgres's change log and seals the difference.

cases.title: Trigger fan-out: the agent reports 1 row, Postgres commits 301
cases.expected: MISMATCH (L2: rows outside the expected footprint)
cases.actual: MISMATCH (L2: rows outside the expected footprint)

cases.title: Trigger changes a column outside the SET list
cases.expected: MISMATCH (L2: column outside the SET list)
cases.actual: MISMATCH (L2: column outside the SET list)

cases.title: Forged deedglass marker from another session, no ledger row (V7 analogue of D01)
cases.expected: DETECTED (forged_marker alert; no action's verdict changes)
cases.actual: DETECTED (forged_marker alert; no action's verdict changes)

cases.title: Write to a watched table without REPLICA IDENTITY FULL
cases.expected: UNVERIFIABLE (replica identity gap; never MISMATCH)
cases.actual: UNVERIFIABLE (replica identity gap; never MISMATCH)

layers.title: Witness (L2): expected and observed
layers.intro: S21's group W: triggers that widen, rewrite or delete, forged and replayed evidence, missing old rows, statements too complex to predict, and a decoder that is late, loses its slot or loses its publication. A gap is UNVERIFIABLE, never MISMATCH; late evidence is an amendment deed, never an edit.

cases.title: The hero: an AFTER trigger ships 300 other orders when one order ships
cases.expected: MISMATCH (L2: Postgres changed 301 rows in public.orders, the agent reported 1; 300 rows outside id = 42)
cases.actual: MISMATCH (L2: Postgres changed 301 rows in public.orders, the agent reported 1; 300 rows outside id = 42)

cases.title: A BEFORE trigger also sets total_cents = 0 on the row the statement names
cases.expected: MISMATCH (L2: a column outside the SET list changed)
cases.actual: MISMATCH (L2: a column outside the SET list changed)

cases.title: A BEFORE trigger rewrites NEW.status to 'cancelled'
cases.expected: MISMATCH at L1 and at L2 (value_mismatch: the committed value isn't the SET literal); the claim is L2
cases.actual: MISMATCH at L1 and at L2 (value_mismatch: the committed value isn't the SET literal); the claim is L2

cases.title: An AFTER trigger deletes another row of public.orders
cases.expected: MISMATCH (L2: a DELETE where the statement only updates rows)
cases.actual: MISMATCH (L2: a DELETE where the statement only updates rows)

cases.title: Another session emits a transactional deedglass marker naming a live action
cases.expected: DETECTED (forged_marker frame and a decoder.alert); the live action is L2 · VERIFIED from its own frame
cases.actual: DETECTED (forged_marker frame and a decoder.alert); the live action is L2 · VERIFIED from its own frame

cases.title: A superuser writes a second ledger row and marker for an action
cases.expected: MISMATCH (L2: multiple_transactions), as an amendment deed when the action was already sealed
cases.actual: MISMATCH (L2: multiple_transactions), as an amendment deed when the action was already sealed

cases.title: REPLICA IDENTITY DEFAULT on the target table, a clean update, verify: L2
cases.expected: UNVERIFIABLE (L2 gap old_image_missing); never MISMATCH
cases.actual: UNVERIFIABLE (L2 gap old_image_missing); never MISMATCH

cases.title: The W01 trigger on a REPLICA IDENTITY DEFAULT table
cases.expected: MISMATCH (L2: row_count_exceeded; the violation beats the old_image_missing gap)
cases.actual: MISMATCH (L2: row_count_exceeded; the violation beats the old_image_missing gap)

cases.title: UPDATE … FROM another table, verify: L2
cases.expected: UNVERIFIABLE (L2 gap footprint_unknown; the claim follows the required level); never MISMATCH
cases.actual: UNVERIFIABLE (L2 gap footprint_unknown; the claim follows the required level); never MISMATCH

cases.title: The decoder is held back, the action seals at the L2 timeout, then the decoder catches up
cases.expected: Action deed UNVERIFIABLE (l2_timeout); then an amendment deed L2 · VERIFIED that amends it; the chain verifies
cases.actual: Action deed UNVERIFIABLE (l2_timeout); then an amendment deed L2 · VERIFIED that amends it; the chain verifies

cases.title: The replication slot is dropped while an action waits for L2
cases.expected: UNVERIFIABLE (L2 gap slot_dropped); never MISMATCH
cases.actual: UNVERIFIABLE (L2 gap slot_dropped); never MISMATCH

cases.title: deedglass_pub dropped and re-created around an action (PG 18)
cases.expected: UNVERIFIABLE (L2 gap publication_gap); never MISMATCH
cases.actual: UNVERIFIABLE (L2 gap publication_gap); never MISMATCH

cases.title: A ledger row whose sql_digest differs from the authorized SQL (a simulated compromised path)
cases.expected: MISMATCH (L2: ledger_mismatch naming sql_digest, never the values)
cases.actual: MISMATCH (L2: ledger_mismatch naming sql_digest, never the values)

layers.title: Approvals, links and webhooks
layers.intro: S22's group L. A person's countersign is the control here, so each case tries to get one without the right person: a replayed email link, a second vote from the same person, the person the action runs for, an agent key, a vote after the approval expired, a vote on an out-of-date view. Then a webhook aimed at cloud metadata, and a forged webhook signature.

cases.title: Approval link replay: the emailed link used again after it approved
cases.expected: REJECTED (approval_link_invalid on every reuse; the action ran once)
cases.actual: REJECTED (approval_link_invalid on every reuse; the action ran once)

cases.title: Another approver's token: a link presented after its owner already countersigned a four-eyes approval
cases.expected: REJECTED (approval_link_invalid or already_countersigned; the approval stays at 1 of 2 and nothing runs)
cases.actual: REJECTED (approval_link_invalid or already_countersigned; the approval stays at 1 of 2 and nothing runs)

cases.title: Self-approval through Deedglass-On-Behalf-Of naming the approver
cases.expected: REJECTED (self_approval; nothing runs until another approver countersigns)
cases.actual: REJECTED (self_approval; nothing runs until another approver countersigns)

cases.title: An agent key approving its own action
cases.expected: REJECTED (approval_needs_person; the approval stays pending and nothing runs)
cases.actual: REJECTED (approval_needs_person; the approval stays pending and nothing runs)

cases.title: A decision after the approval expired
cases.expected: REJECTED (approval_expired; nothing runs)
cases.actual: REJECTED (approval_expired; nothing runs)

cases.title: A decision on a stale context digest
cases.expected: REJECTED (context_changed; the approval stays pending and nothing runs)
cases.actual: REJECTED (context_changed; the approval stays pending and nothing runs)

cases.title: A webhook URL to the cloud metadata service
cases.expected: BLOCKED (destination_blocked at create; 0 deliveries)
cases.actual: BLOCKED (destination_blocked at create; 0 deliveries)

cases.title: A forged webhook signature checked with webhook.Verify
cases.expected: REJECTED (ErrSignature for a wrong secret or changed body; ErrTimestamp outside 300 s)
cases.actual: REJECTED (ErrSignature for a wrong secret or changed body; ErrTimestamp outside 300 s)

layers.title: Undo
layers.intro: S23's group U. An undo writes to the customer's database on a person's request, so each case tries to make it write something Postgres didn't record, or to reach it without a person: rows that change under it, values smuggled into the request, a forged marker naming the action, an agent calling the internal tool, another org's action.

cases.title: An undo whose rows change between the preview and the run
cases.expected: REJECTED (undo_conflict; the undo is failed and Postgres changed no row)
cases.actual: REJECTED (undo_conflict; the undo is failed and Postgres changed no row)

cases.title: An undo request that smuggles values or a tampered plan digest
cases.expected: REJECTED (validation_failed for any field beyond plan_digest, reason, allow_triggers and wait; undo_plan_stale for a digest Deedglass didn't plan; no row changes)
cases.actual: REJECTED (validation_failed for any field beyond plan_digest, reason, allow_triggers and wait; undo_plan_stale for a digest Deedglass didn't plan; no row changes)

cases.title: An undo of an action after a forged marker names it in another transaction
cases.expected: REJECTED (the forged transaction never becomes evidence: the plan holds only the action's own bound transaction, and the forged rows stay as they are)
cases.actual: REJECTED (the forged transaction never becomes evidence: the plan holds only the action's own bound transaction, and the forged rows stay as they are)

cases.title: An agent calling the internal undo tool through POST /v1/actions
cases.expected: DENIED (tool_unknown, recorded and sealed; nothing reaches Postgres)
cases.actual: DENIED (tool_unknown, recorded and sealed; nothing reaches Postgres)

cases.title: An undo of another org's action
cases.expected: REJECTED (not_found for preview and run, exactly as an unknown id; nothing is planned)
cases.actual: REJECTED (not_found for preview and run, exactly as an unknown id; nothing is planned)

not_covered: How often models fall for injections. These cases start after the model was fooled.
A compromised Deedglass host, database superuser or seal key.
Malicious upstream behaviour beyond tool naming: tool descriptions that carry instructions, poisoned results, slow-drip responses (S34).
Denial of service at scale. J04 checks one agent's budget, not a flood.
The supply chain beyond `govulncheck` (S35 adds the SBOM and container scanning).
The V0 cases not listed as running above.
What L2 can't see: effects outside Postgres, writes to tables outside the publication, and proxy-mode SQL servers (no marker to bind). `docs/WITNESS.md` lists them.

Production network rules for private ranges: the suite runs in dev with the private-network override so it can reach its own loopback servers. Metadata, link-local and cross-host targets stay blocked even then (K01, K02); the prod-only rules are covered by the egress corpus (`internal/connector/egress`).
